modern_restatement_en: Count the permutations $\sigma$ of $\{1,\dots,8\}$ such that $|\sigma(i)-\sigma(j)|\ne |i-j|$ for all $i\ne j$. These are exactly the placements of 8 non-attacking queens on an $8\times8$ board. The answer is 92, falling into 12 classes under the symmetries of the square.
well_posed_note: The difference condition must be read in absolute value, and 'arrangement' means a permutation. Under that reading the problem is exactly the eight queens problem.

elementary_check.plan: Backtrack over all placements. Check that the given arrangement 1 7 5 8 2 4 6 3 is valid. PASS if the count is 92 and there are 12 orbits under the dihedral group.

belief.note: The answer of 92 was given by Nauck (1850) and discussed by Gauss. Günther and Glaisher (1874) gave determinant-style proofs, and Lucas's Récréations treat it. Its listing as 'unsolved' only reflects that no solution was printed in the journal.
